name: User Accounts (ProfileList)
purpose: Identifies both local and domain accounts that have interactively logged on to the system, by enumerating one subkey per user SID with a pointer to that user's profile folder.
key_fields: ProfileImagePath value - the filesystem path to that account's profile folder
SID structure - the RID suffix identifies well-known accounts (e.g., -500 for the built-in Administrator) independent of any display-name rename
normal_baseline: Subkeys correspond only to expected local and domain accounts known to have legitimately logged onto the machine, with ProfileImagePath values pointing to standard C:\Users\<name> paths.
anomalies: A new SID/profile subkey appearing shortly before or during an incident for an account absent from the organization's identity system
ProfileImagePath pointing to a nonstandard location outside the normal C:\Users tree
A profile subkey present with no corresponding active local or Active Directory account, consistent with an account that has since been deleted while its ProfileList entry persisted
A domain SID mapped under ProfileList that doesn't correspond to the domain the asset records show this host as joined to
anti_forensic_notes: Deleting a local user account does not automatically remove its ProfileList subkey or profile folder, so a stale entry can remain as evidence of a since-deleted account; conversely, an attacker who manually deletes both the ProfileList subkey and the profile folder can attempt to hide that an account ever logged on locally, though this can still leave traces in the sam-hive or security-eventlog.
interpretation: ProfileList is useful for mapping a SID to its account name; each subkey is named for a user's SID and contains a ProfileImagePath value indicating that user's profile path. Well-known SID RID suffixes (e.g., -500 for the built-in Administrator) can help identify privileged accounts even after a display-name rename.
